::: proof
With the canonical link,
the natural parameter of observation $i$ is its linear predictor:

$$
\ba
\theta_i &= g(\mu_i)
&& \text{(definition of the canonical link)}
\\ &= \eta(\vx_i)
&& \text{(definition of the link function)}
\\ &= \tp{\vx_i}\vb
&& \text{(definition of the linear predictor)}
\ea
$$

The log-likelihood contribution of observation $i$ is

$$
\llik_i(\vb)
\eqdef \frac{y_i \theta_i - b(\theta_i)}{\phi} + c(y_i, \phi),
$$

and its derivative with respect to $\theta_i$ is

$$
\ba
\deriv{\theta_i} \llik_i
&= \frac{y_i - b'(\theta_i)}{\phi}
&& \text{(differentiate term by term)}
\\ &= \frac{y_i - \mu_i}{\phi}
&& \text{(the mean is } b'(\theta_i)\text{)}
\ea
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

The derivative of $\theta_i = \tp{\vx_i}\vb$ with respect to $\vb$ is the vector
$\ub{\vx_i}_{(p+1) \times 1}$.
So, by the chain rule:

$$
\ba
\ub{\deriv{\vb} \llik_i}_{(p+1) \times 1}
&= \ub{\deriv{\vb} \theta_i}_{(p+1) \times 1} \ub{\deriv{\theta_i} \llik_i}_{1 \times 1}
&& \text{(chain rule)}
\\ &= \vx_i \frac{y_i - \mu_i}{\phi}
&& \text{(substitute both derivatives)}
\ea
$$

The outcomes are independent,
so the log-likelihood is the sum $\llik(\vb) = \sumin \llik_i(\vb)$, and:

$$
\ba
\scorev(\vb)
&= \sumin \deriv{\vb} \llik_i
&& \text{(derivative of a sum)}
\\ &= \sumin \vx_i \frac{y_i - \mu_i}{\phi}
&& \text{(substitute each term)}
\\ &= \frac{1}{\phi} \sumin \vx_i (y_i - \mu_i)
&& \text{(factor out } 1/\phi\text{)}
\ea
$$
:::
